notes: Matched-agent parity (Scenario 3: the original benchmark uses a custom agent). Both sides run ContractBench's own tool-calling loop: natively in the original harness (agents/docker_runner.py at the original_parity_repo revision), and in Harbor as contractbench-parity-agent@1.0.0 (src/contractbench/parity_agent.py), a port that keeps the system prompt, bash tool definition, temperature 0.0, max_tokens 16384, 30 model calls, the soft deadline (600 s, matching the original side's run_task_docker.py --timeout 600), 60 s per-command limit and 30,000-character output truncation. Original side: run on 2026-09-02 requesting openai/gpt-4o; the harness does not record the resolved model, and Harbor trajectories from the same day and API key record gpt-4o-2024-08-06 as the model serving that alias. Harbor side: run on 2026-10-27 requesting gpt-4o-2024-08-06 explicitly; every response reports gpt-4o-2024-08-06. Scored trials: original 99/99, Harbor 99/99. Per-task: no task is solved on only one side; 28 of 33 tasks have identical pass counts across the 3 runs and the other 5 differ by one run. Order followed on the Harbor side: 6-task sanity check, one full run, then two more full runs. The 3 Harbor trials of retry-backoff-compliance first ran at the upstream default 300 s deadline, reached it and scored 0; they were rerun at 600 s and again scored 0 (ending at the 30-call cap like the original side). No other Harbor trial reached 300 s. Harbor-side cost $15.49 (sanity check, 3 runs and the 3 rerun trials, from recorded token usage); original side about $22 at list price from logged token counts.
